paragraph.text: G13. "I know someone who got sick being vegan"

one case doesn't refute the reviews and positions of nutrition bodies, and what really happened is rarely known. Often the diet was poorly planned, lacked B12 or energy, there was another health problem, or there was an eating disorder, sometimes predating the diet and hidden behind it. A poorly planned vegan diet can do harm, just like a poorly planned diet with meat: common omnivorous diets are linked to millions of deaths a year worldwide. Each case needs to be investigated, not turned into a general conclusion. The problem is planning, not the absence of meat.
"My cousin got sick. An influencer quit veganism for health reasons. I saw an ex-vegan's story."
I know people who got sick or felt unwell being vegan.
They got better when they went back to eating meat.
This indicates the vegan diet doesn't work for everyone.
So the vegan diet is risky.
P1 and P2 may be true. The problem lies in P3: individual cases don't show the cause, and improvement may come from any change in diet, such as more energy, more variety or correcting a deficiency.
as a testimony. It fails as proof about the vegan diet in general.
"An influencer quit veganism for health reasons."
"I was vegan for 5 years and nearly died."
"There are documented cases of serious deficiencies in vegans."
"She got way too thin after going vegan."

Sometimes someone gets sick while eating in a new way and thinks the new way is to blame. But maybe they were missing a vitamin or eating too little. Sometimes the person was already ill before, or was afraid of eating, and that's an illness that needs a doctor. Many people who eat meat also get sick because of their food. A person who eats only bread also gets sick, but no one says the problem is not eating meat. That's why we need to find out what really happened. The important thing is to eat well and eat a variety of foods.

I'm sorry about your cousin. But one case doesn't show the cause: often the diet was poorly planned, lacked B12 or energy, or there was another problem, including an eating disorder that sometimes shows up under the name of "veganism". A Faunalytics survey of former vegetarians and vegans showed that most gave up within the first year, many without supervision. Many people also get sick on common omnivorous diets: a large study linked dietary risks, such as too little whole grain and fruit and too much sodium, to 11 million deaths in 2017, and no one concludes from one case that meat is dangerous. Each case needs to be investigated, and nutrition bodies show that a well-planned vegan diet is adequate. What happened to her deserves care, but it doesn't change the question: if we can live well without it, what justifies making animals suffer and die?
"Was she supervised by a dietitian, and was she taking B12?"
The personal case has many possible explanations:
Is it the lack of meat?
No: it's lack of a supplement
A diet based on few foods
An earlier or hidden eating disorder
No: it's an illness that can use the diet as an accepted way to restrict
The effect of expectations or social stress
Individual cases don't show the cause of anything. Reviews and the positions of nutrition bodies are based on many studies (D4).
Whoever tells the story almost never knows whether there was supervision, blood tests or supplementation.

text.bold: 3. Sometimes the problem is an eating disorder.

paragraph.text: Eating disorders are serious illnesses, and restrictive eating sometimes presents itself as "veganism" or "vegetarianism", because it's a socially accepted way to eat less. In a study of women who had had an eating disorder, most of those who became vegetarian saw the diet as related to the disorder, and it began after it (G20). In these cases, the cause of the illness is the disorder, and the person needs treatment, not a debate about meat.

text.bold: 4. Many people get sick on common omnivorous diets.

paragraph.text: A Global Burden of Disease study, published in

in 2019, estimated that dietary risks were linked to about 11 million deaths worldwide in 2017, mostly from cardiovascular disease; the leading factors were too much sodium, too little whole grain and too little fruit. No one concludes from one case that every diet with meat is dangerous; the same caution applies to the vegan diet.

text.bold: 5. Each case needs to be investigated.

paragraph.text: Faced with someone who got sick, the right thing is to ask what happened: were there blood tests, B12, enough energy, supervision? Was there a disorder, an earlier illness, another cause? Without that investigation, the case supports no general conclusion, for or against the diet.

The Faunalytics survey showed that most former vegetarians and vegans gave up within the first year, and many within three months. The main reasons included dissatisfaction with the food, health and social issues.

text.bold: 7. Getting better after a change doesn't prove the cause.

paragraph.text: Whoever goes back to eating meat usually also starts eating more and more varied food. The improvement may come from that.
"Ex-vegan" stories attract attention and sometimes come with sales of products or diets. That doesn't make them false, but it shows that the cases that circulate most don't represent everyone.

(d) The strongest counter-reply: some people find it harder
The most serious version grants that individual cases prove nothing in general, but says some people, because of health conditions or individual factors, may find a vegan diet harder.
(e) Why the counter-reply doesn't reach the conclusion

text.bold: That justifies exceptions, not the rule.

paragraph.text: Veganism already allows for what is "possible and practicable" (D7).
Many difficulties are solved with professional guidance.

text.bold: Most people aren't in that situation.

paragraph.text: Often, whoever repeats someone else's story has never tried.

A sad case doesn't change what the evidence shows, and even real cases of difficulty justify exceptions at most. For most people, the moral question remains: if we can live well without killing animals, why carry on?

paragraph.text: And doesn't conclude meat is dangerous.

paragraph.text: But draws a general conclusion from it.
One known case weighs more than statistics
Negative cases are remembered; positive ones, forgotten
The principle being tested is: "if someone got sick on a diet, the diet is dangerous".
They'd be dangerous, because many people get sick on them
It would be dangerous, because some people get hurt
It would be dangerous, because someone had a side effect

Cases of people who had problems being vegan exist, and should be taken seriously. They show that information and supervision are essential, and that animal advocates should speak clearly about B12, energy and variety.

But one case isn't a rule, and each case needs to be investigated. What these stories show, most of the time, is the importance of planning, and sometimes of treating an eating disorder, not the need to eat animals.
